bib.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; qualitative example tables (Table 9, Fig 2-6 transcripts) read lightly.

question: Can instruction tuning be extended to the language-image space by using language-only GPT-4 to generate multimodal instruction-following data, and does a model tuned on it follow visual instructions?
hypothesis: Machine-generated (GPT-assisted) language-image instruction data, as in text-only instruction tuning, improves a connected vision encoder + LLM's instruction following (implied).
contributions: Multimodal instruction-following data: a pipeline converting image-text pairs into instruction format with ChatGPT/GPT-4
Large multimodal model: CLIP visual encoder connected to Vicuna, fine-tuned end-to-end; with GPT-4 ensemble SoTA on ScienceQA
Multimodal instruction-following benchmark: LLaVA-Bench (COCO and In-the-Wild)
Open-source release of generated data, code, checkpoints and a visual chat demo

method.summary: A trainable linear projection maps CLIP ViT-L/14 grid features into the word-embedding space of Vicuna. Stage 1 trains only the projection on 595K filtered CC3M caption pairs; stage 2 fine-tunes projection and LLM on 158K GPT-4-generated instruction samples (or ScienceQA). GPT-4 sees only captions and bounding boxes, never pixels, when generating the data.

datasets.name: CC3M filtered (CC-595K)
datasets.preprocessing: Spacy noun-phrase extraction; skip noun-phrases with frequency < 3; from lowest-frequency noun-phrase add captions to pool; if frequency > 100 randomly keep 100 captions; unique noun-phrases 108182 -> 31423. Converted to single-turn instructions with a random brief-description question, caption as answer.

datasets.name: LLaVA-Instruct-158K
datasets.size: 158K samples (58K conversation, 23K detailed description, 77K complex reasoning)
datasets.source: COCO images; generated by GPT-4 (ChatGPT ablated early) from 5 captions and bounding boxes with few-shot in-context examples
datasets.preprocessing: Per type a few manually designed seed examples; detailed description: one question randomly sampled from a curated list per image; conversation is multi-turn, other two single-turn, sampled uniformly in training. About 80K unique images per Table 3 text.

datasets.name: ScienceQA
datasets.preprocessing: Single-turn conversation: question and context as instruction, reasoning and answer as response.

datasets.name: LLaVA-Bench (COCO)
datasets.source: random COCO-Val-2014 images; 3 question types per image generated with the data pipeline

datasets.name: LLaVA-Bench (In-the-Wild)
datasets.source: indoor/outdoor scenes, memes, paintings, sketches; manually curated detailed description per image

models.name: LLaVA
models.architecture: CLIP ViT-L/14 encoder + linear projection W + Vicuna decoder
models.init_from: CLIP ViT-L/14 and Vicuna (Vicuna-v0 system message)

other.visual_features: grid features before the last Transformer layer (best) vs after
other.connector: single trainable linear projection, Hv = W . Zv
other.frozen: vision encoder always; LLM frozen in stage 1

other.also: judge and reference answerer on LLaVA-Bench, ensemble partner on ScienceQA

training.objective: auto-regressive next-token likelihood on assistant answer tokens (and stop token ###) only, conditioned on image and instruction; stage 1 trains W only, stage 2 trains W and LLM
training.regularisation: FSDP and gradient checkpointing (memory saving, no offloading)
training.wall_clock: stage 1 within 4 hours; stage 2 on Instruct-158K within 10 hours; ScienceQA fine-tune within 4 hours

inference.samples: LLaVA-Bench In-the-Wild: three inference runs for first three rows (mean +/- std); LLaVA dagger: one set of decodings judged by GPT-4 three times
inference.prompting: GPT-4 on ScienceQA: 2-shot in-context learning; judge scheme: when LLaVA and GPT-4 disagree, GPT-4 is prompted again with the question and both outcomes

metrics.name: relative score (LLaVA-Bench)
metrics.definition: text-only GPT-4 judge rates helpfulness, relevance, accuracy and level of detail of candidate answer and of a reference text-only GPT-4 answer (given ground-truth captions/descriptions) on 1-10; reported as candidate score relative to the reference

eval.protocol: GPT-4 as judge; judge prompt text not given in the paper; no significance test; std over 3 runs for In-the-Wild baselines

availability.code: released; anonymized GitHub at time of submission, project page https://llava-vl.github.io

prompts.purpose: generate image-based conversation data with ChatGPT/GPT-4
prompts.text:
You are an AI visual assistant, and you are seeing a single image. What you see are provided with five sentences, describing the same image you are looking at. Answer all questions as you are seeing the image.
Design a conversation between you and a person asking about this photo. The answers should be in a tone that a visual AI assistant is seeing the image and answering the question. Ask diverse questions and give corresponding answers.
Include questions asking about the visual content of the image, including the object types, counting the objects, object actions, object locations, relative positions between objects, etc. Only include questions that have definite answers: (1) one can see the content in the image that the question asks about and can answer confidently; (2) one can determine confidently from the image that it is not in the image. Do not ask any question that cannot be answered confidently.
Also include complex questions that are relevant to the content in the image, for example, asking about background knowledge of the objects in the image, asking to discuss about events happening in the image, etc. Again, do not ask about uncertain details. Provide detailed answers when answering complex questions. For example, give detailed examples or reasoning steps to make the content more convincing and well-organized. You can include multiple paragraphs if necessary.
prompts.where: Appendix F, Table 13 (few-shot examples in Tables 15, 16; detailed-description and complex-reasoning prompts only in the codebase)

evidence.quote: pre-train our model on the filtered CC-595K subset for 1 epoch with a learning rate of 2e-3 and a batch size of 128

results.claim: Full-data LLaVA reaches 85.1% relative score vs text-only GPT-4 on LLaVA-Bench (COCO).
results.setup: LLaVA-Bench (COCO), 30 images/90 questions, trained on all three data types
results.quote: Finally, we show that having all three types of data yields the best performance at 85.1%.

results.claim: Without instruction tuning the relative score drops to 21.5%.
results.table: Table 4, row No Instruction Tuning, column All

results.claim: Conversation-only data gives 73.8%, 11.3 points below full data.
On In-the-Wild LLaVA scores 67.3% overall and 81.7% on complex reasoning relative to text-only GPT-4.
results.setup: LLaVA-Bench (In-the-Wild), 24 images/60 questions, mean over 3 runs (std 2.0)
results.quote: Compared to the text-only GPT-4 that has access to ground-truth labels, LLaVA achieves an impressive 81.7% performance on complex reasoning questions, with an overall score of 67.3%.

results.claim: LLaVA beats BLIP-2 by 29 points and OpenFlamingo by 48 points on In-the-Wild.
results.quote: Thanks to visual instruction tuning, LLaVA achieves significantly better performance compared with BLIP-2 (+29%) and OpenFlamingo (+48%).

results.claim: Fine-tuned on ScienceQA, LLaVA alone gets 90.92%, near MM-CoT Large SoTA.
results.setup: ScienceQA test, 13B, visual features before last layer, reasoning then answer, 12 epochs
results.quote: It yields 90.92% accuracy, which is quite close to the SoTA 91.68%.

results.claim: LLaVA + GPT-4 as judge sets new SoTA 92.53% on ScienceQA.
results.setup: ScienceQA test; GPT-4 re-prompted with both answers when it disagrees with LLaVA
results.quote: achieves a new SoTA accuracy of 92.53%

results.claim: Text-only GPT-4 2-shot gets 82.69% on ScienceQA vs 75.17% for GPT-3.5 CoT.
results.quote: achieve 82.69% accuracy, which is a 7.52% absolute gain compared with 75.17% from GPT-3.5

results.claim: GPT-4 complement scheme (fallback to LLaVA) gives 90.97%, almost no gain over LLaVA alone.
results.quote: This schemes yields 90.97% accuracy, which is almost the same as applying our method alone.

results.claim: Skipping stage-1 pre-training drops ScienceQA accuracy to 85.81%.
results.setup: ScienceQA, trained from scratch on ScienceQA, vs 90.92 best
results.quote: We skip pre-training and directly train on Science QA from scratch – performance drops to 85.81% accuracy.
This yields 89.84% accuracy, which is 1.08% lower than 90.92%

results.claim: Using last-layer CLIP features gives 89.96%, 0.96 lower than the pre-last-layer features.
results.quote: which yields 89.96% and is 0.96% lower than the feature before the last layer

results.claim: Answer-first ordering reaches 89.77%; reasoning-first converges in 6 epochs to 89.77% but adds little to final accuracy.
results.quote: answer-first reports the best number 89.77% accuracy in 12 epochs
results.note: Paper text says answer-first is 'best number' yet Table 8 shows it 1.15 below the best variant (reasoning-first, 90.92); wording is loose.

results.claim: Training cost is small: stage 1 on CC-595K completes within 4 hours on 8x A100.
results.quote: Pretraining on CC-595K completes within 4 hours.

results.claim: Stage 2 on Instruct-158K completes within 10 hours on 8x A100.
results.quote: Finetuning on Instruct-158K completes within 10 hours.

results.claim: Text-only GPT-4 gave higher-quality instruction data than ChatGPT (e.g. spatial reasoning) in early ablations; no numbers given.
LLaVA sometimes treats an image as a 'bag of patches' (says yes to strawberry yogurt in a fridge holding only yogurt and strawberries).

limits: Judge is text-only GPT-4 given captions/descriptions, so evaluation is by a model that never sees the image; robustness of this judge not tested (Appendix A).
Training images are COCO and CC3M only; instruction data derived from captions and boxes so quality bounded by those annotations.
LLaVA-Bench is tiny: 30 images/90 questions and 24 images/60 questions.
Single linear projection explored; gated cross-attention and Q-former left as future work.
Hallucination, bias from CLIP and Vicuna, and high-resolution / knowledge coverage failures conceded.
Academic-benchmark results deferred to the follow-up (Liu et al. improved baselines); the Vicuna base version beyond 'Vicuna-v0' system message, decoding settings and seeds are not stated.
Ablation on data mix is run with one training run each; no variance for Table 4.
